Flag crisis periods

Source: R/date-utils.R
is_crisis_period.Rd

Flags the crisis episodes of either published analysis. windows = "wai" (the default) marks dates inside the two windows used by the Weekly Activity Index analysis; windows = "fcast" marks target quarters inside the four windows used by the out-of-sample evaluation of Eckert, Kronenberg, Mikosch & Neuwirth (2025).

Usage

is_crisis_period(date_vec, windows = c("wai", "fcast"))

Arguments

date_vec

Periods to classify. For windows = "wai" a Date vector (or coercible). For windows = "fcast" a numeric vector of target quarters in decimal time, e.g. 2020.25 for 2020Q2.

windows

Which crisis definition to apply: "wai" (default) for the date-based windows of the Weekly Activity Index analysis, or "fcast" for the quarter-based windows of Eckert et al. (2025).

Value

Logical vector, TRUE for periods inside a crisis window.

Details

The two definitions are not interchangeable, which is why the choice is an explicit argument rather than something a caller can drift past. They differ in two ways, both of which matter:

What is classified

"wai" takes the date the nowcast was made, as a Date. "fcast" takes the target quarter being nowcast, as decimal time (2020.25 for 2020Q2) – the period column of the evaluation panel. In a real-time evaluation those are weeks or months apart, so the two label different rows.

Which episodes

"wai" covers the global financial crisis (2008-07-07 to 2009-09-28) and Covid-19 (2020-01-01 to 2021-12-28). "fcast" adds the euro crisis and the 2015 Swiss franc shock, and its windows are quarters rather than days.

Measured on the paper's own evaluation panel, the two agree on only 124 of its 240 crisis dates, and using "wai" where "fcast" is meant does not reproduce the published figures: crisis RMSFE for the monthly benchmark comes out at 0.0262 against the 0.0210 the "fcast" definition gives, which is what the paper plots.

Before version 0.1.0.9000 the "fcast" windows lived in a second exported function, is_crisis_period_fcast(). Two exported functions for one concept with different hard-coded windows is exactly the parity problem the windows argument removes; is_crisis_period(x, windows = "fcast") replaces it.

References

Eckert, F., Kronenberg, P., Mikosch, H., & Neuwirth, S. (2025). Tracking economic activity with alternative high-frequency data. Journal of Applied Econometrics, 40(3), 270-290. doi:10.1002/jae.3104

Examples

is_crisis_period(as.Date(c("2015-01-01", "2020-06-01")))
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE

# the Eckert et al. (2025) windows, on target quarters in decimal time:
# 2020Q1-2021Q3 are crisis quarters, 2019 and 2022 are not
is_crisis_period(c(2019, 2020, 2021.25, 2022), windows = "fcast")
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE  TRUE FALSE

# and the two genuinely differ -- 2012 is a crisis quarter only for "fcast"
is_crisis_period(2012, windows = "fcast")
#> [1] TRUE
is_crisis_period(as.Date("2012-06-01"))
#> [1] FALSE
